app.title: CORN | Corpus-Oriented Relationship Notation
app.summary: A person sets up a project from a CSV or SQLite table of documents: they choose the ID, text and title fields, the metadata filters, a fixed set of relationship (tie) labels and optional typed attributes. They then filter the corpus to a set of matching documents and open one. They select a passage in the text to create a source-to-target relationship with a label, an exact evidence span, a note and attribute values, and save each document's annotations under their own workspace and annotator scope. They can also queue LLM annotation jobs over the same documents and copy an LLM result into their own editor to revise it. They can compare one human scope with one model's output as precision, recall, F1, a confusion matrix and attribute agreement, and export everything as an edge-list CSV or a JSON archive.

task.text: Code the relationships between named entities in each document of a corpus as labelled, evidence-backed ties, and check machine-generated ties against a human coder's.

data.text: A corpus of text documents with metadata columns, loaded from a CSV or SQLite table. Each document gets a list of directed source-to-target entries. Each entry carries one or more labelled ties drawn from a fixed tie schema, with an exact evidence span, a free-text note and optional categorical, numeric or temporal attributes. These come from human annotators and from LLM runs.
data.item: a document in the corpus, with its relationship annotations

stage.text: coding relationships in a document corpus against an agreed tie schema, then comparing model coding with human coding

mechanism.text: Sidebar filters run a query that fills a table of matching documents. The chosen document opens in a reader beside an annotation panel. Selecting text in the reader opens a dialog that creates a relationship entry. A button on any tie switches the reader into span-capture mode, so the next selection fills that tie's evidence. Saved spans are drawn back into the reader as coloured highlights with hover tooltips, and 'Locate in document' scrolls to them. A separate reporting panel scores one human scope against one LLM scope, and sidebar exports write the annotations out.

field.text: relationship coding of text corpora into networks, in the social sciences

workflow.name: apply labels from a fixed scheme to stretches of text across a corpus, and score automatic labelling against a human's

steps.here: A guided wizard inspects a CSV or SQLite source. The person maps the ID, text and title fields, picks metadata filter types, defines tie labels and typed tie attributes, and builds a runtime cache. A YAML or JSON config can be uploaded instead.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: The person picks a workspace and annotator, sets the metadata filters and the annotation-status and LLM-status filters, then presses Run query. This fills a 'Matching documents' table to choose from.

steps.step: select a stretch and label it with a category
steps.here: Selecting text in the document reader shows a floating action that opens a 'Create annotation entry' dialog. The dialog takes a source node, a target node and a tie type. 'Select span from document' re-captures evidence for an existing tie, and when the span text matches in several places the person picks the right one.

The annotation panel lists every entry and tie, each with a span, a note and an Attributes expander validated against the schema. Saved spans show as coloured highlights in the reader with tooltips, and 'Locate in document' scrolls to and focuses the span.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: LLM annotation tools queue jobs for the current document or the whole query result, using an editable prompt template and a Gemini, OpenRouter or Ollama model. Any LLM run can be viewed or duplicated into the human editor for revision.

steps.step: find where people disagree and resolve it
steps.here: The LLM reporting panel sets one human (workspace, annotator) scope against one provider/model scope, directed or undirected. It reports precision, recall, F1, macro F1, per-label metrics, a confusion matrix with a 'none' class, and attribute agreement.

Pending annotations for every changed document are saved together from the sidebar. Exports write all, human, LLM or human-from-LLM annotations as an edge-list CSV or a JSON ZIP, and a single document's annotation can be exported or imported as JSON with strict validation.

distinctive: Each annotation is a directed source-to-target relationship holding one or more typed ties, so the coded corpus can be exported straight away as a network edge list.
Every tie must have evidence: an exact character-offset span in the document or a free-text note. A tie without a resolved span is saved but flagged 'Needs span review'.
The tie scheme and its typed attributes (categorical options, numeric range, partial ISO date periods) are fixed when the project is set up and enforced on save, on LLM output and on import.
LLM coding runs as queued background jobs. The human coder works from LLM results by duplicating them into an editor marked 'human_from_llm'.

Agreement is measured on deduplicated (source, target, label) tuples per document. The human scope defines the evaluation set, and a coverage control decides whether documents the model never ran on count against recall.

parts.title: Researcher scope and filters sidebar
parts.summary: The person picks a workspace and annotator, filters the corpus by metadata, annotation status and LLM status, runs the query, and rebuilds the project cache.

parts.title: Matching documents table
parts.summary: Shows the documents that match the query with their metadata and annotation status, and lets the person choose one to open.

parts.title: Document reader with span selection
parts.summary: Shows the document text with its saved evidence spans as coloured highlights and hover tooltips. A text selection either creates a new entry or fills the span of the tie waiting for one.

parts.title: Create annotation entry dialog
parts.summary: Turns the selected passage into a new relationship entry once the person gives a source node, a target node and a tie type from the schema.

parts.title: Annotation panel
parts.summary: Lets the person choose a human or LLM annotation record for the document and edit each entry's nodes and ties, including label, span, note and validated attributes. Ties can be re-pointed at a new span or located in the text, and LLM results can be duplicated into the human editor.

parts.title: LLM annotation tools
parts.summary: The person edits and saves the prompt template, previews the rendered prompt, picks a provider and model, queues annotation jobs for this document or the whole query result, and watches or cancels recent jobs.

parts.title: LLM reporting panel
parts.summary: Scores one human annotator scope against one LLM provider/model scope, directed or undirected. It shows precision, recall, F1, per-label metrics, a confusion matrix and attribute agreement.

parts.title: Save, export and import
parts.summary: Saves pending annotations for every changed document, exports a chosen annotation scope as an edge-list CSV or JSON ZIP, and exports or imports one document's annotation as JSON.
